method: Tokenized C use sites exclude comments, strings, and macro definitions. Unused macros and address-only/projection uses are not scalar-byte findings.

Native records come only from function-associated exported instruction lists in pinned dossiers/cache. Every instruction byte is authenticated against the PE; no linear disassembly over gaps creates a function.
Matching source/global width and native read width is candidate evidence, not proof of exact source-to-instruction equivalence or mechanical patch safety.

Register-variable scans distinguish dereference stores (pointer reads), direct assignment, initializer and address escape. Source-definite missing initialization is separate from control-flow heuristic leads.
C prototypes/calls are balanced-token parsed. Unspecified argument lists do not imply zero native arguments.
Partial AL writes require whole native return dataflow and caller-consumer audits. Original code identity tokens do not by themselves indicate original execution.
limitations: This is a static triage tool, not a C AST/CFG verifier or function acceptance suite. Conditional initialization, macros, adapters and noncanonical native ABIs need manual/native review.
Absence of native evidence is reported explicitly and never filled by disassembling until the next guessed entry.
Counts describe the source hashes captured here; concurrent source changes require rerunning the audit.
